taxonomyNote: NatureServe (Phuong et al. 2014) splits the northern lineage as O. douglasii, narrowing O. beecheyi; Animal Diversity Web uses Spermophilus beecheyi and an older, wider range.
fieldMarks: Mottled gray, light and dark brown and white, with a darker mantle and lighter gray shoulders and neck
Bushy tail in the same mixed colours
behavior: Diurnal; sunbathes; stays close to its burrow
Lives in loose burrow colonies; most of a population may be yearlings
May hibernate or aestivate depending on climate; active all day in warm weather
Omnivorous, mostly green vegetation in spring and seeds, berries and nuts later; cheek pouches to carry food
habitat: Open areas in many plant communities from fields and grasslands to mountains; avoids deserts.
range: North-central California and west-central Nevada south to Baja California.

lookalikes.name: Douglas's ground squirrel
lookalikes.howToTell: The northern lineage formerly included in this species, now treated by NatureServe as O. douglasii.
